posts.text:
The best UX designers I know aren't using Figma AI.

They're ignoring it completely.

And honestly? They're making a mistake.

I spent the last two weeks embedding AI features into my design workflow. Not because it's trendy. Because I was genuinely curious if it could replace the parts of design work I actually hate.

The result surprised me.

Figma AI didn't make me a better designer. It made me a faster strategist.

Here's what actually works:

**Auto Layout suggestions cut my component building time by 40%**

I used to spend 20 minutes tweaking spacing and constraints. Now AI suggests the structure, I validate it in 30 seconds, move on. The creative work starts earlier.

**Content generation for realistic prototypes**

No more lorem ipsum or spending time writing fake product descriptions. The AI populates realistic user scenarios instantly. My stakeholder demos went from "I guess this could work" to "when can we ship this?"

**Visual search across design systems**

I can describe a pattern ("mobile checkout flow with Apple Pay") and it surfaces similar components across our entire library. This alone has saved our team from rebuilding the same components three times.

But here's the contrarian part everyone's missing:

The designers winning with AI aren't the ones automating their taste. They're automating the scaffolding so they can spend more time on the decisions that actually matter.

AI can't tell you if your user flow respects someone's time. It can't identify the emotional gap in your onboarding. It can't sense when a feature is solving the wrong problem.

It can make the boring parts disappear so you have more space to think about those things.

The future of UX isn't "AI vs designers." It's designers who use AI to do less UI work and more user thinking.

Most teams are using Figma AI to move faster.

The best teams are using it to think deeper.

Follow me.

I think most people are using AI completely wrong.

They're using AI to save minutes.

The real opportunity is using AI to build products, businesses, and income streams.

Over the last few weeks, I've been exploring different AI tools, and one platform genuinely surprised me: Emergent.

Instead of helping you write better prompts, it helps you move from idea → prototype → product much faster.

As a Product Designer, what caught my attention wasn't the technology.

It was the speed.

The gap between:
💡 "I have an idea"

and

🚀 "I have something people can actually use"

is shrinking faster than most people realise.

We're entering a world where solo builders can compete with teams.

That's a massive shift.

I'm currently experimenting with Emergent and exploring how AI can accelerate product design, MVP creation, and business building.

If you're curious, here's my invite link:
https://lnkd.in/gEMRsAdj

Now I'm curious:

👉 What is the ONE AI tool that has genuinely changed the way you work this year?

#AI #ProductDesign #UXDesign #BuildInPublic #ArtificialIntelligence #Designpreneur #Startups #IndieHackers #FutureOfWork

Most AI design tools try to replace designers.
That’s why they fail.
After testing Anthropic's and Claude Design, one thing stood out:
👉 It doesn’t fight your process. It works with it.
Instead of generating final screens, it focuses on:
• Prototyping first
 • Working with your system
 • Supporting your thinking
But let’s be real:
Design system bridge = promising, not perfect
Portability = still messy
Biggest blocker? Your Figma file 👀
Hard truth:
AI won’t fix bad design systems.
 It will expose them.
This is the first AI tool that feels built with designers, not just for them.
Early days. But directionally right.
Have you tried it yet — hype or actually useful? 👇

Coming up with 6 different layout ideas used to take a full afternoon.
Now I get them in 15 minutes—then pick and polish the best one.

I was designing an onboarding flow and needed several layout directions to test with stakeholders. I wanted variety fast—not polished final screens. So I used a Figma AI plugin and a prompt-based image generator for visual variations.

Then I tried AI:-
1- Write a short brief: user goal, tone, and brand constraints.
2- Prompt AI (Figma plugin): “Generate 6 low-fi wireframe suggestions for a 3-step onboarding flow.”
3- Generate microcopy with ChatGPT for each screen (1-line headings, 2-line description, CTA).
4- Create quick visuals (AI image generator for hero images and placeholders).
5- Pick the top 2 ideas, refine by hand, then test with colleagues.

Results:-
⏳ Before: 3–4 layout concepts in 3–4 hours.
⚡ After: 6 rapid concepts in 15–20 minutes; 1 solid prototype ready in under 90 minutes.
💡 Impact: Faster iteration, more creative options, and stakeholders loved seeing choices early.

A caution: AI sometimes invents weird UI elements or nonexistent icons. I always do a sanity pass and adjust spacing, accessibility, and real copy.

Takeaway:
AI helps with ideation and speed. It amplifies your creativity—but your critical eye keeps the design real.

#UIDesign #AIDesign #Figma #UXDesign #Productivity

Today, I'm sharing a step-by-step guide to the future of AI-driven UX

(after analyzing 10+ AI interfaces and their impact on user experience)

Follow these simple yet effective steps to prepare for the buttonless, screenless future of user interaction:

- Embrace Conversational Design
No more clicking or tapping. Users will simply speak their needs. Transform your UI from visual hierarchies to natural dialogue flows.

- Master Context-Aware Responses
Design AI responses that understand user intent, emotion, and urgency. The interface becomes invisible, but the experience becomes more human.

- Build Trust Through Intelligence
Create AI interactions that feel natural yet secure. Focus on tone, personality, and ethical boundaries that make users comfortable with AI handling their tasks.

- Optimize for Universal Access
Design voice-first experiences that work for everyone. When screens disappear, accessibility becomes universal through natural conversation.

From embracing conversational design to optimizing for universal access, each stage is designed to help you create more intuitive, human-centered AI experiences.

Take action and watch your progress soar! 💪

#AIinUX #FutureofDesign #UXDesign #ConversationalAI
